clue.text: Dismiss shipping channel that circumvents US state

indicators.note: a channel that goes round something encloses it, so the state's letters sit inside

parts.note: a seaway is a route for ocean-going ships, such as the St Lawrence Seaway
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: Someone waves off a shipping route that skirts round an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone off is to tell them to leave, a phrasal synonym for dismissing them.

clue.text: Unexpectedly release from prison sentence (about 13 weeks)

parts.note: to spring a prisoner is to free them suddenly, as in a jailbreak
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A convict is suddenly freed partway through a sentence of about three months.
explanation.definitionFit: A season lasts roughly a quarter of a year, which is about thirteen weeks.

clue.text: Almost drunk carrying plate and candle

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

indicators.note: the drunk word holds the plate letter inside it

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
L as on the L-plate a British learner driver must display

explanation.surface: A tipsy waiter nearly drops a plate and a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small squat candle burnt in a holder, giving gentle light through the dark hours.

clue.text: Partner inhaling oxygen mixture

indicators.note: breathing in takes the gas inside the partner word

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A companion breathes in an oxygen blend.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal made by combining two or more elements is a mixture, like brass or bronze.

clue.text: An aria a slut's performing from "South Pacific"

indicators.note: the letters are put through their paces into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies a letter here

explanation.surface: A showgirl sings a solo from the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges ANARIAASLUTS; 'South Pacific' is the musical, but read here as the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Australasia covers Australia, New Zealand and nearby islands of the southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: What's coughed up for saying nothing (almost) about backup

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so the silent word encloses the backup
the silent word loses its last letter, falling just short of complete

parts.note: stumm (also shtum) is slang for keeping quiet
read as back-up: the word up written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone stays almost silent when asked about their reserve plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the slang word for silent, and 'about' wraps it round 'backup' read as two words, up turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the phlegm and mucus brought up from the lungs by coughing, so it is literally what is coughed up.

clue.text: Foul in penalty zone that shouldn't be visible

indicators.note: a foul shot is badly made, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a foul committed in the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' shuffles INPENALTY; the football surface hides lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: The outline of underwear seen through tight clothing is something wearers prefer to keep unseen.

clue.text: Largely agree such a story is implausible

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Most people concur that such a yarn is hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims TALLY to its first four letters; 'such a story is' hints at a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story or tale is one that is exaggerated and hard to believe.

clue.text: Note in old currency

definitions.meaning: to note something is to take notice of or record it
the Deutschmark, German money before the euro

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to note something and the former currency unit of Germany.

clue.text: Finely wrinkled mat on which Uruguay get beaten

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the following pieces are placed after the mat, joined on to it

parts.note: a rug is a small floor mat
U is the international vehicle registration code for Uruguay
to lose is to be beaten in a match

explanation.surface: A football match played on a rug sees Uruguay defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical and zoological term for a surface covered in fine wrinkles, as on some leaves.

clue.text: Strong feelings about student hobbyist

indicators.note: the feelings go around the student, enclosing that letter

parts.note: anger is a strong feeling of displeasure
L stands for learner, as on a British L-plate for learner drivers

explanation.surface: Someone has intense emotions towards a student who pursues a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fishes with rod and line, usually for pleasure, is a classic example of a hobbyist.

clue.text: Composer not quite admitting singer's right to one rare instrument

indicators.note: the composer lets the other pieces in, enclosing them
the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Johann or Richard Strauss
a diva is a celebrated female singer; the possessive adds nothing
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A nearly complete composer lets a singer have the right to one precious violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' removes the composer's final letter; the waltz-king surface hides that the singer, right and one all go inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin or cello made by Antonio Stradivari, among the rarest and most valuable instruments.

clue.text: Infested with bits — bits that really matter

parts.note: nitty means infested with nits, the eggs of lice
gritty means full of bits of grit

explanation.surface: Something crawling with small particles, the parts that count.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'bits' first means particles of grit, then the essential details.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the basic, essential details of a matter, the core facts that count most.

clue.text: King and country collecting tipsy toper's familiar pieces

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the country takes the jumbled drinker inside

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

indicators.note: drunkenly unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: Monarch and nation gather round a drunk's favourite songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's stock of works they know and can play is their repertoire.

clue.text: Electronic digger crossing stream in light footwear

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: the digger lies across the stream, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a spade is a digging tool
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A robotic excavator crosses a brook in summer shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shoe with a rope sole, a light summer footwear from Spain.

clue.text: Unexpected development in dance

definitions.meaning: a plot turn that surprises, as in a story's ending
a rock and roll dance popularised by Chubby Checker in the early 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a surprising turn of events and a 1960s dance with swivelling hips.

clue.text: Hiding hasty penetration of object

indicators.note: the hasty word pierces into the object word

parts.note: a thing is an object
rash means hasty or reckless

explanation.surface: Something is hidden by a quick thrust into an object.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a beating, and a thrashing is the same kind of punishment.

clue.text: Not so great a penalty incurred for luxuriant growth

indicators.note: the penalty is taken inside, as if run into by the outer word

parts.note: less means smaller, not so great
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: Being charged a fine reduces one's standing, though it brings lush greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incurred' plays on being run into: the penalty and its article end up inside the word for not so great.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant leaves make a plant look lush, so a state of being covered in foliage is luxuriant growth.

clue.text: Scholar caustic about one-on-one religious teacher

indicators.note: the second one is placed on, after, the preceding pieces

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate or scholar

indicators.note: the harsh word goes around one, enclosing that letter

parts.note: harsh means severe or cutting, like a caustic remark
the Roman numeral I is one
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A learned person makes a cutting remark about one-to-one tuition from a spiritual guide.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a maharishi is a great sage or spiritual guide, hence a religious teacher.

clue.text: Unpleasant treatment partially reversing lameness

indicators.note: the selected letters are read from right to left
only part of the word lameness is taken

explanation.surface: A painful medical procedure partly cures a limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes AMENE from inside 'lameness' and 'reversing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An injection of fluid into the rectum is a medical treatment most find disagreeable.

clue.text: Impale a spud, stifling beginning of Mary's hymn

parts.note: to stab is to pierce, as when impaling

indicators.note: the potato wraps round and smothers the letter

parts.note: tater, like spud, is slang for a potato

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Skewering a potato while suppressing the start of a hymn to the Virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval Latin hymn on the sorrows of Mary at the Cross, set by many composers.

clue.text: Painter got up two hours before midday

indicators.note: in a down entry the time is written upwards

parts.note: ten am is two hours before noon

explanation.surface: An artist rose at ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns TENAM upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French painter, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Animals raised to be vocal

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down entry the word is written upwards

parts.note: gnus are wildebeest

explanation.surface: Livestock are brought up to be noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is sung is vocal music, so the word describes voiced performance.

clue.text: North African territory unlikely to be cultivated

definitions.meaning: a Muslim of Berber and Arab descent from north-west Africa
open uncultivated upland covered with heather

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Berber Muslim of the Maghreb and an expanse of wild heathland.

clue.text: First-rate drug available to all, retrospectively, in an ideal world

indicators.note: looking back, so the run of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
pot is slang for cannabis
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: In a perfect society top-quality cannabis would be on hand for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns the whole run AIPOTU round; A1 is taken with the digit as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imagined island gave its name to any perfect society, an ideal world.

clue.text: Undone twice in Elba — or twice in four years?

indicators.note: the letters are loosened and rearranged
the word in is taken two times

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is twice brought low on Elba, like Napoleon in exile.
explanation.definitionFit: An event that happens every second year occurs twice in a four-year period.

clue.text: Musical genre's rubbish — no heart to it

indicators.note: the middle letter of the rubbish word is removed

parts.note: garbage is rubbish or refuse

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a style of music as trash lacking soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no heart to it' drops B, the middle letter of seven-letter GARBAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of electronic dance music that grew from house in the 1980s and 1990s.

clue.text: One annoyed about the consistent summer temperature

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the annoyed word goes around the following word

parts.note: sore is informal for irritated or annoyed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated about the unchanging summer heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a map joining places with equal mean summer temperature, so a uniform summer warmth.
